setup.why: Control: confirm prod tag-listing works for this project before probing the capability under test, and get a sense of the real tag vocabulary.

attempts.changed: Documented-valid empty array. Bare unshaped 500 - not the declared {success,tags,error_tags,error} 200 shape, and not the declared {success:false,error:{code,message,details}} error envelope either. Identical body to the preprod failure for this exact capability.

Mixed payload: one real, already-used tag ('sprint1', confirmed present in setup) plus one disposable, obviously-synthetic wording. Same bare 500, byte-identical body to attempt 1 - payload-independent, exactly as on preprod.

Single new (unused) tag wording alone. Same bare 500, byte-identical body to attempts 1-2. Three distinct payload shapes (empty array, mixed known+new, single new), three identical 500s - confirms this is a deterministic handler-level fault, not sensitive to array contents or length.

notes:
PREPROD vs PROD, side by side: PREPROD verdict for verify_test_case_tags was BLOCKED - all 5 attempts (a real known-used tag + a new one, an identical retry, a rejected non-integer project_id control, the documented-valid empty tags:[], and an ordinary tag wording) returned an identical bare {"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error"} instead of the declared 200 shape, while the sibling list_test_case_tags succeeded against the same project_id in the same window (ruling out an outage or bad id). PROD: the block REPRODUCES exactly, with the identical bare body. Ran 3 attempts here (empty tags:[] per the contract's documented-valid case, a mixed known+new tag payload, and a single new-tag payload) - all three returned status 500 with the exact same literal body {"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error"}, never the declared {success,tags,error_tags,error} 200 shape and never the declared {success:false,error:{code,message,details}} error envelope either. The control call (list_test_case_tags, same project_id 332537, same session) returned 200 with real data, so this is not an outage, not a bad project id, and not a prod-only artifact - it reproduces the preprod fault verbatim, including the exact error body text.

Shared-shape question: is this the same family as list_tags's test_recording 500 or list_test_case_tags's q-filter 500? Partial match. All three share the defining characteristic of being a BARE, framework-level 500 that does not conform to either declared response schema (success or the app's {success:false,error:{code,message,details}} envelope) and that reproduces deterministically regardless of otherwise-valid payload/query variation - i.e. all three are handler-level crashes exposed as raw server errors rather than caught application errors. However the literal JSON body differs between families: verify_test_case_tags on both preprod and prod returns {"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error"}, while list_tags's test_recording crash (re-probed on prod separately, see tests/live/runs/tm-prod/list_tags.json) returns a differently-shaped body {"type":"server_error","message":"Internal Server Error"} with a stable ETag across retries. I did not independently re-invoke list_test_case_tags with a q filter in this probe (out of scope for verify_test_case_tags's contract, which takes no q param), so I can't confirm its exact error body shape here - going only on the task's description of it as a bare 500. So: same underlying pattern (uncaught handler-level 500, non-declared shape, payload-independent) but not byte-identical error bodies across capabilities - each looks like its own uncaught exception surfacing through a generic error path rather than all three sharing one literal error renderer. Recommend routing verify_test_case_tags's prod block to the product team as a confirmed-live production defect, same as was done for list_tags's test_recording case.
